scenes.tts: An organoid has no blood. Every bit of oxygen must diffuse in from its surface. What happens at the center?
scenes.visual: Title card: Measured Against Fetal Cortex. An organoid sphere with no vessels; small oxygen dots at its surface. Question: what happens at the center?
scenes.narration: An organoid has no blood. Every bit of oxygen must diffuse in from its surface. What happens at the center?

scenes.tts: The cells use oxygen as it moves inward. So it runs out a short way in.
scenes.visual: Oxygen dots move inward and are consumed; a colour gradient forms from bright at the surface to dark inside.
scenes.narration: The cells use oxygen as it moves inward. So it runs out a short way in.

scenes.tts: Take a simple model, with assumed rates of oxygen use. In a large organoid, oxygen reaches only about zero point one to zero point six millimetres in.
scenes.visual: On screen: in this model, oxygen reaches about 0.1 to 0.6 mm into a large organoid. Assumptions shown small: uniform tissue at steady state; surface oxygen fixed at 100 to 200 micromolar (assumed); oxygen use from the adult brain's rate down to a tenth of it (assumed). Model numbers, not measurements.
scenes.narration: Take a simple model, with assumed rates of oxygen use. In a large organoid, oxygen reaches only about 0.1 to 0.6 millimetres in.
scenes.caption: Take a simple model, with assumed rates of oxygen use. In a large organoid, oxygen reaches only about 0.1 to 0.6 millimetres in.

scenes.tts: A large organoid is up to about four millimetres across. In this model, a third or more of it has no oxygen.
scenes.caption: A large organoid is up to about 4 millimetres across. In this model, a third or more of it has no oxygen.
scenes.visual: The sphere is labelled up to about 4 mm across. The dark core is shaded and labelled no oxygen in this model: about a third to four fifths of the volume.
scenes.narration: A large organoid is up to about 4 millimetres across. In this model, a third or more of it has no oxygen.

scenes.tts: That is why cells in the center of a large organoid often die.
scenes.visual: Cells in the dark core turn grey and break up.
scenes.narration: That is why cells in the center of a large organoid often die.

scenes.tts: In adult cortex, capillaries sit only tens of micrometres apart.
scenes.visual: Inset: adult cortex threaded with capillaries, labelled tens of micrometres apart.
scenes.narration: In adult cortex, capillaries sit only tens of micrometres apart.

scenes.tts: Faster spinning helps only partly. It keeps the surface supplied, but under these assumptions it cannot feed a deep core.
scenes.visual: The sphere spins faster; the bright outer shell holds steady but the dark core stays dark.
scenes.narration: Faster spinning helps only partly. It keeps the surface supplied, but under these assumptions it cannot feed a deep core.

scenes.tts: Shortening the path helps. Slice the organoid, or grow it where air meets liquid.
scenes.visual: A thin slice of organoid on a membrane at an air–liquid interface, bright throughout.
scenes.narration: Shortening the path helps. Slice the organoid, or grow it where air meets liquid.

scenes.tts: Blood is surroundings. The rule flags this failure, and the estimate shows how large it is.
scenes.visual: Rule card in amber: blood is surroundings, flagged to fail.
scenes.narration: Blood is surroundings. The rule flags this failure, and the estimate shows how large it is.

scenes.tts: Now a finer test, cell by cell. Do the organoid's cells match fetal cortex?
scenes.visual: Two columns of cell clusters, one labelled organoid, one labelled fetal cortex, with a question mark between them.
scenes.narration: Now a finer test, cell by cell. Do the organoid's cells match fetal cortex?

scenes.tts: Single-cell R N A sequencing counts the messenger R N As in thousands of separate cells.
scenes.caption: Single-cell RNA sequencing counts the messenger RNAs in thousands of separate cells.
scenes.visual: Single cells pass one by one through a counter; each emits a bar code of messenger RNA counts.
scenes.narration: Single-cell RNA sequencing counts the messenger RNAs in thousands of separate cells.

scenes.tts: Cells with similar profiles are grouped into clusters. Then each organoid cluster is compared with each fetal one.
scenes.visual: Dots gather into coloured clusters in both columns.
scenes.narration: Cells with similar profiles are grouped into clusters. Then each organoid cluster is compared with each fetal one.

scenes.tts: In twenty twenty, Aparna Bhaduri and colleagues compared hundreds of thousands of cells this way.
scenes.caption: In 2020, Aparna Bhaduri and colleagues compared hundreds of thousands of cells this way.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Bhaduri, Andrews, Kriegstein and colleagues, 2020. About 235,000 organoid cells; about 189,000 cells from developing human cortex.
scenes.narration: In 2020, Aparna Bhaduri and colleagues compared hundreds of thousands of cells this way.

scenes.tts: The broad classes matched: radial glia, intermediate progenitors and neurons. Those are program features, as the rule predicts.
scenes.visual: Teal bands join matching classes in the two columns: radial glia, intermediate progenitors, neurons. Small label: broad classes recognizable; proportions can differ.
scenes.narration: The broad classes matched: radial glia, intermediate progenitors and neurons. Those are program features, as the rule predicts.

scenes.tts: Finer subtypes blurred. An organoid cluster often resembled several fetal subtypes about equally.
scenes.visual: One organoid cluster sends equal, blurred bands to three fetal subtype clusters, labelled identity blurred.
scenes.narration: Finer subtypes blurred. An organoid cluster often resembled several fetal subtypes about equally.

scenes.tts: Markers of particular subtypes, such as sat B two in upper-layer neurons, were much rarer.
scenes.caption: Markers of particular subtypes, such as SATB2 in upper-layer neurons, were much rarer.
scenes.visual: A bar for SATB2 upper-layer neurons, much shorter in the organoid column than in the fetal column.
scenes.narration: Markers of particular subtypes, such as SATB2 in upper-layer neurons, were much rarer.

scenes.tts: Here is the twist. Organoid cells expressed stress genes at higher levels.
scenes.visual: A stress-gene meter reads high over the organoid column. Labels: glycolysis, endoplasmic reticulum stress.
scenes.narration: Here is the twist. Organoid cells expressed stress genes at higher levels.

scenes.tts: Transplanted into mouse cortex, those stress genes fell. Some cells came to resemble fetal subtypes more closely.
scenes.visual: Organoid cells move into a mouse cortex outline; the meter drops and one blurred arrow sharpens onto a single subtype.
scenes.narration: Transplanted into mouse cortex, those stress genes fell. Some cells came to resemble fetal subtypes more closely.

scenes.tts: So the dish itself seems to add problems.
scenes.visual: Label over the dish: culture seems to add stress.
scenes.narration: So the dish itself seems to add problems.

scenes.tts: The rule says where to look first. It is not a verdict. Every feature still has to be measured.
scenes.visual: Closing card: the rule says where to look first, not what you will find. Measure every feature.
scenes.narration: The rule says where to look first. It is not a verdict. Every feature still has to be measured.
